html:
SMTO-UI-0009 — SMTO couldn't confirm your approval choice was saved

GUID: 37c2db83-75a1-4aeb-ae99-c7ad221066de
Slug: ui-permission-save-failed
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • You made an approve or deny choice for a waiting task, but the page never got confirmation that SMTO saved it. It may or may not have been saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: refresh the browser page, open the conversation, and see whether the task is still waiting for approval or has moved on. The choice may have been saved even though the page didn't receive the confirmation.
  2. If the task has moved on, or you see Approval recorded, don't choose again; your decision was saved. Making the choice a second time could apply a permission twice or change a decision that already took effect.
  3. Only if the task still asks for approval, make your choice once and wait until the task moves on. If you had chosen Keep current policy when asked to allow globally, nothing was saved. Waiting for one choice to finish avoids sending two decisions for the same request.

What success looks like

  • The task stops asking for approval and continues, or it shows as stopped if you denied it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep clicking approve or deny while you're unsure whether the first choice was saved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Approval handling received a false result from submitConfirmation, so the browser cannot confirm the server accepted the permission decision.

What this means

  • Approval handling receives a false result from submitConfirmation and cannot confirm that the policy decision was accepted. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Approval handling receives a false result from submitConfirmation and cannot confirm that the policy decision was accepted.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the exact pending approval and retained decision before pressing approve again.

How to fix it

  • submitConfirmation (app.js) returns false when a decision for the same request is already in flight, when the user cancels the 'Allow operations globally' confirmation, or when the POST to /api/agent/confirmation/<request> fails (shown as a toast); it returns no value after the server records the approval without a continuation request_id ('Approval recorded' toast), which approvePolicy also reports as this error. Reload the run, check its status and saved permission decision, and submit a new decision only if none was recorded.
  • Refresh the current approval and inspect its saved decision before submitting another action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • One saved decision is shown for the current approval identity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
